items.bold: MOJTABA KHAMENEI FULL STATEMENT: "Americans belong at the bottom of the Persian Gulf waters." New chapter declared.
items.text: Times of Israel (15hr ago), Business Standard, The Week, and Geo.tv all confirmed Mojtaba Khamenei's full Persian Gulf Day statement — his most extensive communication since becoming Supreme Leader. Key quotes (all verified): "The only place Americans belong in the Persian Gulf is at the bottom of its waters." "By God's help and power, the bright future of the Persian Gulf region will be a future without America." "Today, two months after the largest military deployment and aggression by the world's bullies in the region, and the United States' disgraceful defeat in its plans, a new chapter is unfolding for the Persian Gulf and the Strait of Hormuz." He also said Iran would maintain Hormuz control and Iran's "new management" of the strait "will bring calm, progress and economic benefits to all Gulf nations." Khamenei is still not seen in public — the statement was read by a state television anchor. Times of Israel: "He seemed to signal Iran would maintain control over the waterway, which lies within Iran's and Oman's territorial waters."

items.bold: IRGC AEROSPACE COMMANDER MOUSAVI: "Long and painful strikes" on US bases/warships if attacks resume.
items.text: NewsNation and CBS News confirmed: Iran's IRGC Aerospace Force Commander Majid Mousavi warned that if the US renewed attacks, Iran would launch "long and painful strikes" against US positions. Mousavi said even limited US strikes would trigger "a broader response across the region" — including targeting US military assets, regional bases, and warships. This is the most explicit Iranian military threat since the ceasefire began on April 8. Combined with Mojtaba Khamenei's "bottom of the waters" statement and Ghalibaf's "future free from American presence" comment — Iran's political, military, and supreme leadership are all aligned on a maximalist position. The IRGC Aerospace Command threat is specifically designed to deter the CENTCOM military options briefing Trump received Thursday — Iran is signalling the cost of any resumed strikes.

items.bold: Mojtaba's HORMUZ DOCTRINE: "New management will bring calm." Permanent Iranian sovereignty — not temporary war tactic.
items.text: The Week confirmed the full Hormuz doctrine statement: Mojtaba Khamenei said Iran's "new management" of the Strait of Hormuz would bring calm, progress and economic benefits to all Gulf nations. Ghalibaf (Parliament Speaker, CBS/Geo.tv): Iran's Hormuz control would allow Tehran to "provide itself and its neighbours with the precious blessing of a future free from American presence and interference." This is critically important: Iran's Supreme Leader is no longer describing Hormuz control as a wartime tactic. He is describing it as permanent doctrine — "new management" of Hormuz is Iran's stated long-term strategic goal. Times of Israel: "Iran had been charging some ships reportedly $2 million apiece to travel through the strait." Iran Parliament was drafting a formal law. The toll system, the Larak Island shipping channel, the "new management" rhetoric — all are Iran's vision for the post-war Hormuz, regardless of ceasefire outcome.

items.bold: UN Guterres: Hormuz "strangling the global economy." IEA Birol: "Biggest energy crisis in history." ECB recession warning.
items.text: Geo.tv and CBS News confirmed: UN Secretary-General Guterres said the Hormuz closure is "strangling the global economy" and set out three scenarios — best case (immediate opening): growth decline, inflation rise, "further economic distress"; if constraint drags through midyear: 32 million people into poverty, 45 million "into extreme hunger"; if war grinds on through 2026: "the world will confront the specter of a global recession." IEA Executive Director Fatih Birol at IEA Paris HQ: "The world is facing the biggest energy crisis in history." ECB warned: "The longer the war and high energy prices continue, the stronger is the likely impact on broader inflation and the economy" — ECB sees Germany and Italy at risk of technical recession by end 2026. Goldman Sachs raised Brent forecast to $90 by late 2026 — global inventories drawing at record pace of 11-12 million bbl/day in April.

items.bold: IRAN INTERNET SHUTDOWN: 90 million Iranians offline for most of 2026. Online economy devastated.
items.text: CBS News confirmed: "Iran's 90 million people have been cut off from the internet for most of 2026, one of the world's longest and strictest national shutdowns. That is devastating an online economy that had long defied government restrictions and international sanctions. From fashion to fitness, to advertising and retailers, many have seen their incomes evaporate." Despite the uneasy truce, Iran's rulers have refused to reverse the shutdown they depict as a wartime necessity, but are facing an outcry as it adds to mass job losses from attacks on key industries and the ongoing US blockade of Iranian ports. This detail is significant for understanding Iran's internal pressure: the Iranian people are experiencing not just a war but a total information blackout — adding to the economic pressure that may eventually push the leadership toward a deal, even if the IRGC and the Supreme Leader maintain their hardline public positions.

assessment.body:
Friday 8:15 PM IST. Day 63. The West Asia War's most consequential doctrine statement.

MOJTABA KHAMENEI'S PERSIAN GULF DAY STATEMENT — THE FULL PICTURE
• "The only place Americans belong in the Persian Gulf is at the bottom of its waters"
• "The bright future of the Persian Gulf region will be a future without America"
• "A new chapter is unfolding for the Persian Gulf and the Strait of Hormuz"
• Iran's "new management" of Hormuz "will bring calm, progress and economic benefits"
• Nuclear and missile capabilities are "national assets" — 90 million Iranians will protect them
• Statement read by state TV anchor — Khamenei still not seen in public since Feb 28

WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN ANYTHING ELSE THIS WEEK
• Mojtaba is not describing Hormuz control as a temporary war tactic
• He is declaring it as Iran's PERMANENT STRATEGIC DOCTRINE
• "New management" = Iran's vision for the post-war Hormuz — with Iranian tolls, Iranian control
• This transforms the peace negotiation: it's no longer about "reopening" — it's about what REPLACES the pre-war status quo
• The US, UK, Gulf Arabs, and international shipping law all consider Hormuz an international waterway
• Iran is now formally asserting it's an Iranian sovereign asset

THE IRGC'S DETERRENCE MESSAGE
• Aerospace Commander Mousavi: "long and painful strikes" on US positions if attacks resume
• Even limited US strikes = broader regional response (US bases, warships)
• This is direct response to Thursday's CENTCOM military options briefing to Trump
• Iran is raising the cost of the military option — deterring resumed strikes

THE GLOBAL IMPACT SCALE
• Guterres: Hormuz "strangling the global economy"
• IEA Birol: "The world is facing the biggest energy crisis in history"
• ECB: Germany and Italy face technical recession by end 2026
• Guterres scenario 3 (war through 2026): "global recession"

INDIA AT 8:15 PM DAY 63
• Markets closed (Labour Day)
• Rupee ATL 95.32 — weakest in Indian history
• OMC hike Rs 9-14/L still imminent Monday announcement possible
• Mojtaba "new management" doctrine: India must plan for permanent Iranian Hormuz management
• Desh Garima (Reuters photo, Mumbai) = model for India's future Hormuz access: coordinated and paid
• Monday open will be the first pricing of Mojtaba's statement
• IRGC Mousavi threat: if US strikes resume → Brent $140-150, rupee Rs 100-105, Sensex below 68,000

VERDICT: Day 63 closes with the most strategically significant declaration of the war. Mojtaba Khamenei has announced that Iran's control of the Strait of Hormuz is not a war weapon — it is permanent Iranian policy. "New management" is not a ceasefire term. It is a sovereign claim on the world's most critical energy chokepoint. The West Asia War began as a conflict over Iran's nuclear programme. It is ending — if it ends — as a conflict over who controls the Persian Gulf forever. India wakes up Monday to price that reality.
